Seminar Title:

Assessment of environmental impacts of different mine unit operations on mine workers and the workplaces

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Mining Engineering

Speaker Name:

Dr. Falguni Sarkar

Speaker Type:

Faculty

Venue:

Mining Department Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

15 Oct 2026 5:15 pm

Contact:

6204641962

Abstract:

Mine workers involved in drilling, blasting, mucking/loading, and ore/waste transportation are directly exposed to hazardous environmental aspects generated during mining operations. This study identifies environmental aspects associated with different mine unit operations, evaluates their impact levels, and develops appropriate operational control procedures (OCPs) for reducing workplace risks and protecting workers' health. A field-based investigation was conducted in an Indian trackless underground hard-rock mine. Workplace parameters including respirable dust, noise, diesel particulate matter (DPM), noxious gases, oil spillage and other environmental aspects were investigated. A HAZOP-based impact assessment methodology was applied by considering severity, exposure duration and frequency of exposure. A total of 24 environmental aspects associated with the mine unit operations were identified and assessed. Of these, 12 aspects were classified as significant, with impact levels greater than 15. The assessment identified noise and dust as major significant hazards, with maximum impact levels of 75, while diesel fumes were significant during mucking and transportation and noxious gases were important hazards during blasting. Based on the identified significant aspects, 12 operational control procedures were developed to reduce environmental and occupational risks.
